title: tau setup --json NDJSON event
description: Schema for one line of `tau setup [--json]` output. Setup streams newline-delimited JSON: one event per step — init (config scaffold), completions (shell completion installs), clients (editor ACP wiring), doctor (embedded health report) — plus exactly one terminal verdict_event (always the last line, always "done":true). Step order is fixed: init, completions, clients, doctor, verdict. Removal mode (`tau setup --remove`/`--uninstall`) emits a different fixed sequence: remove_clients (editor wiring reversal), verdict — the verdict carries "remove":true there. Detect mode (`tau setup --detect`) emits detect_clients (read-only client inventory), verdict — the verdict carries "detect":true there. The event types are mutually exclusive — validate each NDJSON line against this schema individually. The process exit code mirrors the verdict's ok (0 when true, 1 when false).

file_preview.description: One file a real run would change, rendered under --dry-run: the exact unified diff that would be applied plus, for in-place rewrites, backup_path — the <path>.bak where the real run preserves the original before overwriting.

action.description: "create" (file absent — the diff reads from /dev/null), "modify" (existing file rewritten — the original lands at backup_path), "delete" (file removed — the diff writes to /dev/null).

diff.description: Unified diff of the current bytes to the would-be bytes (---/+++ headers, @@ hunks, \ No newline markers).

backup_path.description: <path>.bak written by a real run before overwriting an existing file; absent for creates and deletes.

init_event.description: First event: the config scaffold step. status is "created" on a fresh write, "exists" when a config was already present, "would_create" under --dry-run, "failed" when the path could not be resolved or written.

config_path.description: Path of the config file; absent on failure.

provider.description: Provider the scaffold was seeded for; absent on failure.

detected_env_keys.description: Provider API-key env var names found set (names only, never values); absent on failure.

files.description: Under --dry-run: one entry per file this step would create, rewrite, or delete — the exact unified diff plus the <path>.bak a real run would leave on in-place rewrites. Absent when nothing would change.

completions_event.description: Second event: shell completion installs. status is "installed" (covers already-current installs), "would_install" under --dry-run, "skipped" when no shell could be detected, or "failed" when an install errored.

reason.description: Why the step was skipped (e.g. could not detect shell from $SHELL).

hint.description: Remediation hint on skipped steps (re-run with --shell ...).

shells.description: One entry per resolved shell, in resolution order; absent on skipped/failed-to-resolve outcomes.

path.description: Installed completion script path; absent on failure.

rc.description: Rc/profile file the autoload hook was appended to (zsh/pwsh only).

rc_status.description: Outcome of the rc-hook append (zsh/pwsh only).

files.description: Under --dry-run: one entry per file this shell's install would create, rewrite, or delete — the exact unified diff plus the <path>.bak a real run would leave on in-place rewrites. Absent when nothing would change.

clients_event.description: Third event: editor ACP client wiring. Without --client the step is "skipped" and reports detected editor config dirs. status is "installed", "would_install" under --dry-run, "manual" when every client needed a paste-ready snippet, "skipped", or "failed".

hint.description: Remediation hint on skipped steps (re-run with --client ...).

detected.description: Editor config dirs that appear installed; emitted on the skipped (no --client) outcome.

clients.description: One entry per resolved client, in resolution order; absent on skipped/failed-to-resolve outcomes.

path.description: Editor settings file path (direct clients only).

command.description: Absolute tau path written into the client config.

next.description: The in-editor action that finishes the integration.

snippet_path.description: Paste-ready fragment path; emitted on manual outcomes.

reason.description: Why the outcome is manual (existing settings file unparsed or missing the tau entry).

editor_detected.description: Whether the editor's config dir exists; emitted on nvim's always-manual entry.

bridge_path.description: mcacp bridge config path (~/.config/mcacp/mcacp.json); MCP-bridge clients only.

bridge_status.description: Outcome of the bridge-side wiring; MCP-bridge clients only.

bridge_snippet_path.description: Paste-ready bridge fragment when the existing mcacp.json could not be spliced.

bridge_message.description: Failure detail for the bridge-side write.

imported.description: MCP server entries merged into this client's settings file by --import, each with the client it was imported from. Always emitted for MCP-bridge clients under --import (empty when nothing was merged).

name.description: Server entry name as written into the client's server section.

from.description: Supported client whose settings file supplied the entry.

import_skipped.description: MCP server entries or source settings files --import could not merge, each with a reason. Entry-level skips carry "name"; file-level findings (unreadable/unparseable source) omit it.

name.description: Server entry name; absent on file-level findings.

from.description: Supported client whose settings file the entry or finding came from.

reason.description: Why the entry or file was not imported.

files.description: Under --dry-run: one entry per file this client's wiring would create, rewrite, or delete — the exact unified diff plus the <path>.bak a real run would leave on in-place rewrites. Absent when nothing would change.

remove_clients_event.description: Removal-mode step event (`tau setup --remove`/`--uninstall`), emitted where the install stream would put init — the only step event before the verdict. Reverses per-client editor wiring: the tau (or mcacp) entry is spliced out of each settings file without re-rendering, files left with no settings are deleted, setup-generated snippets are cleaned, and the shared mcacp bridge entry is dropped once no client outside the removal set still uses it. --client scopes the sweep; without it every client is processed. status is "removed", "would_remove" under --dry-run, "manual" when nothing was removed but hand-work remains (init-file wiring, unreadable/unparseable files), "absent" when nothing was wired, or "failed".

clients.description: One entry per processed client, in client order; absent on failed-to-resolve outcomes.

path.description: Editor settings file path (direct clients only).

file_deleted.description: The settings file was (or, under --dry-run, would be) deleted entirely — it held no settings besides the tau wiring.

snippet_path.description: Setup-generated snippet file that was cleaned; emitted when a snippet existed.

snippet_status.description: Outcome of the snippet cleanup; emitted with snippet_path.

snippet_message.description: Failure detail for the snippet cleanup.

reason.description: Why the outcome is manual (init-file wiring, unreadable or unparseable settings file).

next.description: The hand-step that finishes the removal; emitted on manual outcomes.

bridge_path.description: mcacp bridge config path (~/.config/mcacp/mcacp.json); MCP-bridge clients only.

bridge_status.description: Outcome of the shared bridge-side entry: kept when another MCP client outside the removal set still uses it.

bridge_file_deleted.description: The bridge config was (or would be) deleted entirely.

bridge_reason.description: Why the bridge entry was kept or needs hand-removal.

bridge_message.description: Failure detail for the bridge-side removal.

bridge_snippet_path.description: mcacp paste-snippet cleaned once the bridge entry went away; emitted when it existed.

bridge_snippet_status.description: Outcome of the bridge snippet cleanup; emitted with bridge_snippet_path.

files.description: Under --dry-run: one entry per file this client's unwiring would rewrite or delete — the exact unified diff plus the <path>.bak a real run would leave on in-place rewrites. Absent when nothing would change.

doctor_event.description: Fourth event: the embedded `tau doctor` health report — the same single-object shape `tau doctor` prints without --json (see docs/doctor-json.md).

detect_clients_event.description: Detect-mode step event (`tau setup --detect`), emitted where the install stream would put init — the only step event before the verdict. A read-only inventory of supported clients: each entry reports the config dir probed, whether the client was detected there, and the wiring state `tau doctor` would classify (settings path and stale reason included when they apply; "bridge":true marks the MCP clients wired through the shared mcacp bridge). --client scopes the sweep; without it every client is listed. Nothing is written. status is "ok" or "failed" (e.g. HOME unset).

clients.description: One entry per surveyed client, in client order; absent on failed-to-resolve outcomes.

detected.description: Whether the client's config dir exists on this machine.

wiring.description: Wiring state as `tau doctor` classifies it: "not_detected" (no config dir), "manual_only" (snippet-only client — Lua/elisp/YAML), "missing_file", "unreadable", "unparseable", "no_entry" (settings file without a tau/mcacp entry), "stale" (broken entry), "ok" (wired).

config_dir.description: Editor config dir probed — the detection anchor.

path.description: Editor settings file path; emitted for JSON clients once detected.

reason.description: What makes the entry broken; emitted with wiring "stale".

bridge.description: Present on MCP-bridge clients — their entry launches the mcacp MCP->ACP bridge, and wiring covers the shared ~/.config/mcacp/mcacp.json side too.

detected.description: How many surveyed clients were detected (config dir exists).

hint.description: Remediation hint emitted when no client was detected.

verdict_event.description: Terminal verdict — always the last NDJSON line, always "done":true. ok mirrors the process exit code (0 when true, 1 when false): any failed step or a failing doctor report flips it.

ok.description: true when every step passed (skipped/manual outcomes still pass).

version.description: tau version that produced the stream, e.g. "0.4.0".

remove.description: Present in removal mode (`tau setup --remove`/`--uninstall`) — the stream then carries only the remove_clients step event and this verdict.

detect.description: Present in detect mode (`tau setup --detect`) — the stream then carries only the detect_clients step event and this verdict.

non_interactive.description: Present when the run was declared unattended (--yes/--non-interactive or env equivalents).

yes.description: Present when --yes approved all write steps.

done.description: End-of-stream marker — true on the verdict line only; the same convention `tau doctor --json` uses.
